protocol.title: PE beads · Exp 02 · Detector photon-transfer curve
protocol.summary: Convert DN to effective photoelectrons for each detector HV with a mean-variance photon-transfer curve, plus offset and read noise.

children.body: Shot-noise SNR, LOD and clipping all need DN converted to photoelectrons.
Pins: g·F (DN per effective photoelectron) at each HV, the offset and the read noise. g and F cannot be separated this way; their product is exactly what SNR needs.
Model: variance(DN) = g·F × (mean − offset) + σ²_read; PMT excess-noise factor F ≈ 1.2–1.5.

rows.free_text: Uniform fluorescent sample in the PE band: orange fluorescent plastic slide, or ≈10 µM rhodamine B in water in a sealed thin chamber

children.body: Acquisition settings

rows.value: 561 nm; 8–10 powers from near zero to ≈80 % of full scale on the brightest pixel
Two single frames per power (no averaging), plus 20 dark frames with the laser at 0 %
512², 2 µs dwell, focus 20 µm into the dye (or on the slide)
Repeat the whole ladder at 4–5 HV values covering what you will ever use

children.body: Before any quantitative acquisition: stand and lasers on for 2–3 h; 561 nm excitation; the same PE emission band (e.g. 570–620 nm) every time; 16-bit with fine integration (the default is 12-bit, so check the file); one HV and one offset for the whole session; background mode at least 50 DN above zero; no saturated pixels. Record the transmitted-light channel with every PE frame: beads are found in it, never in PE. Find focus in transmitted light and hold it with Perfect Focus. Never live-scan PE to focus.
At this HV a pixel reading [!var:dn_reading] holds [!var:e_eff] (SNR [!var:snr_px]); a pixel clips above [!var:e_max].
Dark
Laser at 0 %, same HV and offset you will use: take 20 frames. They give the offset (mean) and read noise (SD).
Ladder
Laser on. At each of 8–10 powers, take two frames in a row without changing anything.
Move the stage 50 µm between powers, so bleaching of a dye slide does not bias the ladder.
Repeat per HV
Repeat steps 01–02 at 4–5 HV values. Keep the offset fixed if NIS allows, or re-measure the dark frames at each HV.
For each frame pair, in a central 256² ROI: m = mean((I₁ + I₂)/2) − offset, and v = var(I₁ − I₂)/2. Taking the difference removes the illumination pattern.
Fit v = slope × m + σ²_read over the unsaturated points. The slope is g·F at that HV. Check that R² is above 0.99.
Tabulate slope against HV. PMT gain is steep (≈ a power of HV), so fit log(slope) against log(HV) to interpolate.

Detector linearity: at the plate HV, mean signal against laser power must stay within 2 % of a straight line up to the photon rate of the top standard's rim. The highest power where it does is the analog linearity limit.
Decision: the HV at which the brightest expected rim pixel stays at or below 60–70 % of full scale (confirmed in Exp 08), and the slope used to convert every later image to photoelectrons.
Record for every acquisition

rows.note: DN per effective e⁻, with R²
Laser % for each rung (µW-equivalent from Exp 01)

children.body: Save the .nd2 files as acquired (no 8-bit export, no LUT) in a folder outside the website repo, e.g. BeadConfocalData/<date>_<exp>/, and fill one plate-map CSV row per well or field (columns are listed in Research/PE_bead_confocal_experiments.md, section 7).
